rows.text: The Monetary Policy Board of the Bank of Korea decided today to raise the Base Rate by 25 basis points, from 1.25% to 1.50%.
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE April 14, 2022
Monetary Policy Decision
Currently available information suggests that inflation has accelerated while the recovery of the global economy has somewhat moderated, affected by the Ukraine crisis.

In global financial markets, government bond yields in major countries have risen sharply and the US dollar has strengthened, mainly due to changes in expectations about the pace of the US Federal Reserve’s policy normalization.

In a related set of actions, the Board has decided to leave the interest rate on the Support Programs for SMEs Affected by COVID-19 and Small Businesses at 0.25%, and to raise the interest rates on the other Programs under the Bank Intermediated Lending Support Facility from 0.25% to 0.50%, effective May 2, 2022.
Stock prices have rebounded after a considerable decline.

Looking ahead, the Board expects that the global economy will resume its trend of recovery, supported by the easing of COVID-19 restrictions in major countries, but sees it as likely to be affected largely by COVID-19 developments, global inflation movements, monetary policy changes in major countries and geopolitical risks.

Background for the Interest Rate Adjustments on the Bank Intermediated Lending Support Facility

The Monetary Policy Board of the Bank of Korea decided to leave the interest rate on the Support Programs for SMEs affected by COVID-19 and Small Businesses at the historic low level of 0.25%, despite raising the Base Rate.
The decision is in consideration of the ongoing difficulties faced by small businesses and SMEs due to the
spread of COVID-19 variants.

The Board decided to raise the interest rates on the other Programs* under the Bank Intermediated Lending Support Facility from 0.25% to 0.50% to be in accordance with the monetary policy stance while maintaining the purpose of the Facility.
* Support Program for Trade Financing, Support Program for New Growth Engine Development and Job Creation, Program for Stabilization of SME Lending, Support Program for Regional SMEs, etc.
The spread between the current Base Rate and the interest rate on the programs is still larger than the spread before the COVID-19 crisis.
* Spread between the Base Rate and the interest rate on the Bank Intermediated Lending Support Facility (bp): (end-2019) 50-75 → (Mar 2020) 50 → (May 2020) 25 → (After Jan 2022) 100
In spite of today’s interest rate adjustments, the Bank’s support for the recovery of vulnerable sectors remains unchanged.
The total ceiling on the Facility and ceilings for the respective programs have not been adjusted.
The Bank will make continuous efforts to provide effective support for SMEs, small businesses and the self-employed through close cooperation with the related agencies.
